mode: image2image (vanilla CSFF card art as style reference)
prompt:
Reference image 1 and reference image 2 are style references only: match their flat posterized colour fills, thin dark ink outlines, small ink tick marks and muted palette; do not copy their subjects.

Subject: a trampled deer lick, a shallow hollow of grey, salty mud where mineral spring water seeps up through the forest floor. The hollow fills most of the lower frame: flattened, damp grey-brown mud pocked and churned by many overlapping deer hoof tracks that cross and recross each other, densest at the centre and trailing off toward the muddy rim. A thin sheen of standing water sits in the lowest dimples. Sparse tufts of grass, a few reeds and scattered pale mineral-crusted stones ring the hollow's edge. Low forest trees and undergrowth frame the background, receding into dim green shade. No deer present, no people, no glowing light.

Style: Card Survival Fantasy Forest game card art. Flat posterized colour fills in a few hard-edged tonal steps, cel-like, no soft gradients, no watercolour bleed, no paper texture, no border or frame. Thin dark ink outlines and small ink hatch and tick marks for texture, used to render the individual hoof tracks clearly in the mud. Muted naturalistic palette of grey-brown mud, moss greens and earth tones. Realistic proportions, nothing glossy, no fantasy glow, no light rays, no text. Full-bleed painted scene filling the whole 2:3 portrait card edge to edge.

Avoid: photo, photorealistic, 3D render, digital vector art, pixel art, neon colors, lens flare, blurry, low contrast, black background, grey solid background, off-white background, gradient background, checkerboard, transparency grid, drop shadow, text, watermark, signature, logo, border, frame, deer or other animals, human figures, sand, snow.
